stories.headline: Carney's unprecedented international travel blitz draws scrutiny and praise
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney has made 47 international trips in his first 100 days in office, triple the usual rate for Canadian PMs. His travels included Nordic summits, meetings with UK PM Starmer, appearances at Davos, and visits to China, India, and other nations as part of a strategy to reduce Canada's dependence on the US.

stories.headline: Poilievre conducts high-profile US tour, appears on Joe Rogan podcast
stories.summary: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre completed his first official US trip, including a widely-watched 2.5-hour appearance on Joe Rogan's podcast, meetings with Texas Governor Greg Abbott, and presentations of his auto sector plan. He used the platform to argue against US tariffs on Canada and defend Canadian sovereignty.

stories.headline: Bank of Canada holds interest rates steady amid Iran war and oil price concerns
stories.summary: The Bank of Canada maintained its key interest rate at 2.25% on March 18, citing the need to assess the economic impact of the Iran war and rising oil prices. Governor Tiff Macklem warned the bank would act if energy price increases become persistent inflation, while also noting weaker-than-expected economic growth.

stories.headline: Carney government releases first budget with significant spending cuts and deficit targets
stories.summary: Prime Minister Carney's first budget outspends the previous Trudeau plan by $67.6 billion over four years while running larger deficits. The budget includes cuts to science, tourism, and foreign aid programs, with plans to reduce waste and government operations spending.

stories.headline: Canadian Armed Forces awarded $307 million contract for new assault rifles
stories.summary: The Defence Investment Agency awarded Colt Canada a $307 million contract to manufacture over 65,000 new rifles to replace the aging C7/C8 assault rifle fleet. The contract is part of the first wave of high-priority defence procurements and will unfold in two phases.

stories.summary: Pascal-Pierre Paillé, who represented Louis-Hébert for the Bloc Québécois from 2008 to 2011, was arrested and charged with sexual assault and sexual contact with minors. The alleged incidents date from 2006 to as recently as August 2024.
